A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RAVENEA and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The benchmark and methods can be matched despite extensive reorganization; reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retriever and downstream evaluations, annotation ablations, geographic analyses, and human evaluation of generated captions.

after.justification: v2 reports revised original evaluations and additional context-control experiments, context-length ablations, and a generated-caption quality study.

M1.justification: The CAC classification, ranking, diversity, and combined losses remain equivalent, using the same CLIP and SigLIP2 backbones. CaCLIP and CaSigLIP2 become Ravenea-CLIP and Ravenea-SigLIP. Changed training schedules and evaluation prompts do not introduce a new retrieval algorithm.

E1.justification: The evaluated CVQA/CCUB tasks, eight countries, and eleven categories remain. v2 adds test conditions containing random characters or unrelated Wikipedia documents from excluded countries (Section 4.2, Table 11). Its newly described 30-country raw collection is not established as expanded training or benchmark evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The seven-retriever comparison is retained after matching renamed methods. v2 adds random-character and unrelated-document comparators in Table 11. The corresponding geographic aggregate comparison narrows from four retrievers in v1 Figures 11–12 to CLIP and Ravenea-CLIP in v2 Figure 10.

E3.justification: Reported CLIP/SigLIP training changes from up to 50 epochs with early stopping to two epochs without it, adding 0.03 warmup (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 9). Maximum generation length increases from 256 to 2048, and caption prompts explicitly require country names. Main evaluation adds Qwen3-VL-2B/8B/32B and replaces InternVL3-38B with 78B-AWQ. Context-control and context-length experiments introduce additional protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds controls testing meaningful cultural context against arbitrary text, paragraph/full-document/top-three-document ablations, and an audit of 50 Chinese-image captions. It also adds annotation-response and missing-document analyses, and revises scaling and geographic comparisons. The qualitative prediction examples in v1 Figure 4 are removed.

E5.justification: The Kendall correlation significance reporting and existing human-agreement procedures remain unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-seed performance uncertainty or confidence intervals. The new caption audit reuses Cohen's kappa reporting; its additional agreement value is a new result rather than a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retrieval and downstream results are extensively revised. CaCLIP/Ravenea-CLIP MRR changes from 78.34 to 82.17. Reported non-RAG/augmented averages change from 67.7/71.5 to 67.1/73.3 for cVQA and from 40.2/58.1 to 57.5/68.8 for cIC (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 3). Settings and model cohorts differ, preventing same-setting improvement claims. Appendix scores, dataset counts, geographic findings, and newly added control results also change.

T1.justification: The CAC equations in v1 Section 4.1 and v2 Section 3.2 are mathematically equivalent. RegionScore moves from v1 Appendix H to v2 Section 3.1 with equivalent notation and definition. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The benchmark, cultural-supervision, retrieval-benefit, and cross-cultural-disparity contributions remain. The abstract recasts v1's minimum gains for lightweight models as average gains across VLMs, approximately +6% and +11%, and expands the stated evaluation from fourteen to seventeen models. The fundamental contribution remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving internalized Wikipedia knowledge, diminishing benefits from longer contexts, and relevant knowledge rather than arbitrary added text. It explicitly positions RegionScore as a complementary geographic-awareness proxy. The ethics discussion adds concrete cultural-misattribution and heritage risks, expert-validation safeguards, and GLAM knowledge sources, beyond the retained coverage and Wikipedia limitations.

D1.justification: Implementation documentation materially changes through revised training settings, generation limits, checkpoint identifiers, and downstream prompt templates. v2 newly documents document-level separation across training, validation, and test splits, the upstream 30-country collection, caption-audit sampling, and random-context construction. The newly disclosed deduplication does not establish that v1 lacked it.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused connections to random-prompt effects through Roth and Ma, socioeconomic evaluation through Nwatu, cultural theory through Yadav, and digital heritage through Münster, alongside model citations. Several introductory application and 3D-vision references disappear. The central positioning around an unmet need for multimodal cultural RAG evaluation remains.

P1.justification: The paper is extensively reorganized and rewritten: related work moves after results, dataset construction gains a taxonomy subsection, methods and evaluation become unified setup/results sections, and findings receive explicit summaries. RegionScore moves into the main text, implementation appendices are consolidated, and terminology and conference formatting change throughout.

P2.justification: v2 replaces introductory examples, simplifies the benchmark overview, redraws scaling and geographic plots, and replaces the split-distribution area chart with bars. It adds context-ablation displays and annotation-quality tables, expands the main results table, relocates dataset statistics, and substantially rearranges appendix figures and prompt tables.

improvement.justification: The new relevance and context-length controls strengthen evidence beyond v1's retrieval comparisons, while the caption audit and clearer data-separation documentation improve scrutiny of benchmark construction. These benefits are tempered by the audit's restriction to 50 Chinese examples and unresolved reporting ambiguities, including 256 tokens versus 256 words and InternVL3-38B versus 78B labels across tables. The revised scores involve changed protocols and cohorts and do not themselves establish better paper quality.
